g.text: What a DBMS is actually doing for you
SQL / query API
what you write
Parser + planner
turns declarative SQL into an execution plan
and picks which index to use
Transaction manager
isolation, locks or MVCC snapshots
Buffer pool
caches hot pages in RAM — most 'disk reads' aren't
Storage engine
B-tree or LSM-tree on disk
Write-ahead log
durability and crash recovery
Disk
The real argument for a database
Every one of these is a thing you would otherwise build.
'Just use files' means writing a planner, a lock manager,
a page cache and a recovery log yourself.
The one dial that matters most
B-tree read-optimised, updates in place Postgres, InnoDB
LSM-tree write-optimised, appends then compacts RocksDB, Cassandra
That single choice explains most performance differences.
